meta.purpose: Every irregularity, gap and open question found during line-by-line verification, across both sessions that worked on this repository. Each item states what was observed, the official source that was checked, the action taken, and whether it blocks publication. Status 'needs review' means the item is published on the Flagged for Review page; it does not block the site going live. Items F-14 to F-24 carry forward findings recorded by the parallel session d14c5409 in REVIEW.md and in the archived data/session-d14c5409/ register; the legacy_ids field on each item gives the id it had there.
meta.id_scheme: F-01 to F-13 were raised by session zone1-main. F-14 to F-24 were carried forward from session d14c5409, either as new findings or as items that that session had raised in a different form; legacy_ids records the original id in the archived register at data/session-d14c5409/flags.json.

sessions.role: Research, verification, data model, static site generator, integration
Repository review, first data pass, first site build, first PR and merge
sessions.status: merged into main via PRs #1, #2 and #3

flags.title: The supplied link.amazon path segments are not ASINs
flags.observation: Each supplied URL looks like it contains an ASIN in its path: link.amazon/B04G1MEwY, link.amazon/B02NbDxp3 and link.amazon/B00hJ57DV. Requesting them over HTTP resolves to three unrelated product pages: /dp/B0CDY277D3 (CHEFMAN 6 Quart Dual Basket Air Fryer Oven), /dp/B09B7SB46R (Emeril Lagasse 26QT French Door Air Fryer Toaster Oven) and /dp/B08DKYBTPH (Chefman Air Fryer 8 Qt TurboFry). The path segment is therefore an opaque redirect token, not the ASIN of the product being promoted.
flags.why_it_matters: Rebuilding the links from the ASIN-looking segment would point every future article at the wrong product. All links in this project are rebuilt from the resolved /dp/<ASIN> destination plus the publisher's tag parameter.
flags.action_taken: Resolved each link, recorded the final URL and the destination page <title> in data/products.json, and rebuilt all outbound links from the resolved ASIN.

flags.title: Amazon renders the used-condition offer without labelling its condition inline
flags.observation: Amazon's buy box for B0CDY277D3 carries exactly two offers. The embedded buy-box payload lists $79.93 with buyingOptionType NEW and $57.45 with buyingOptionType USED. In the rendered price block the second offer appears as "$57.45 with 43 percent savings -43%" and "$28.73 per count", followed by the same "List Price: $99.99" line and the list-price explanatory note about "the suggested retail price of a new product". The condition word USED appears only in the embedded payload, not in the rendered text next to the price, so a reader scanning the page — or a scraper reading the rendered text alone — can reasonably read $57.45 as a second new-condition price. The two offers are also not stable between fetches: the same URL has served different buy-box contents across retrieval windows.
flags.why_it_matters: Publishing $57.45 as a new-condition price would be a false statement about the product and would breach the FTC truthfulness rule for endorsements. Price volatility matters for the same reason: any price quoted on the site is a dated snapshot that must be re-verified before it is republished.
flags.action_taken: The catalogue publishes $79.93 as the new-condition price and $57.45 as the used-condition offer, and states the condition tag Amazon itself applies, with the exact URL it was read from. The misleading second-new-price row was removed from the dataset. The published price snapshot is dated and carries a re-verification schedule on the Campaign page, and the site's standing caveat says plainly that these are dated snapshots of official pages rather than licensed Product Advertising Content.

flags.title: Product 2 detail page serves a reduced body
flags.observation: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B09B7SB46R returned only navigation and footer markup — no buy box, price block, star rating, feature bullets, 'About this item' list, Product information block or Item details block — on six differently-formed requests (/dp/, /gp/aw/d/, /gp/product/, the canonical slug URL, with and without ?psc=1&language=en_US, and with an added qid/sr). The page <title> was served correctly on every request.
flags.why_it_matters: The specification fields that make this product comparable (dimensions, weight, wattage, material, model number, UPC, Best Sellers Rank, warranty, temperature range) could not be read from an official source.
flags.action_taken: The product's title, brand, rating, review count, price, list price, promotion badge, alternative-offer price and monthly purchase volume were verified from Amazon's own search result listing for the ASIN (https://www.amazon.com/s?k=B09B7SB46R) and are recorded with that URL as the source. Every specification field that could not be read is left blank and labelled unverified rather than inferred from the title or from the other two products.

flags.title: The Amazon Associates rate card is not publicly readable
flags.observation: The Program Policies Appendix links Standard Commission Income to https://affiliate-program.amazon.com/help/operating/schedule. Requesting that URL redirects to the Amazon sign-in page (…/home/account/payment/customratecard). No public first-party page states a per-category commission rate for Kitchen & Dining air fryers.
flags.why_it_matters: Commission potential is the core driver of every product decision in an affiliate business, and no honest statement about it can be made from a public source.
flags.action_taken: No numeric commission rate is asserted anywhere on this site. The revenue model on the Research & Analysis page is expressed as commission = price × r, with r supplied by the publisher from their own signed-in rate card, and is shown at a spread of illustrative rate inputs that are labelled as inputs rather than as Amazon's rates.

flags.title: All prices, badges, purchase-volume counts and Best Sellers Ranks are point-in-time
flags.observation: Prices, discount percentages, promotion badges, 'K+ bought in past month' counts and Best Sellers Rank change continuously on Amazon. Every figure in this project was captured on 2026-11-13.
flags.why_it_matters: A stale price in an affiliate article is both a customer-trust problem and a compliance problem under the Program Policies, which require limited-time promotion references to be removed once the promotion ends.
flags.action_taken: Every dynamic value is stamped with its verification date in the catalog tables, and the Campaign & Automation page specifies a scheduled re-verification job and a SiteStripe/PA API replacement for the static price column.

flags.title: Product 1 capacity is rendered in litres on Amazon while the manufacturer states quarts
flags.observation: The Product details block for B0CDY277D3 lists "Capacity | 6 liters". The product title, the manufacturer bullets and the product imagery all describe a 6-quart dual-basket air fryer with 3-quart baskets.
flags.why_it_matters: A comparison table that mixes the two units would misstate the product's size relative to the 8-quart and 26-quart products.
flags.action_taken: Both values are recorded verbatim in separate rows and the unit discrepancy is shown on the row itself; the prose uses the manufacturer's quart figure because that is what the manufacturer states on the page.

flags.title: Program Policies restrict displaying Product prices without Amazon-served or API-sourced data
flags.observation: Program Policies, Participation Requirements section 2(b): "Product prices and availability may vary from time to time… your Site may only show prices and availability if: (a) we serve the link in which that price and availability data are displayed, or (b) you obtain Product pricing and availability data via Creators API or PA API and you comply with the requirements regarding use of Creators API or PA API in the License."
flags.why_it_matters: This site is a static GitHub Pages build with hand-verified price snapshots, which is neither option (a) nor option (b). The prices are therefore research data, not licensed Product Advertising Content.
flags.action_taken: Every price on this site is labelled as a dated research snapshot with the Amazon page it was read from, and the compliance page records two compliant routes before the site is used for live traffic: (1) replace the static price column with SiteStripe or a PA API widget that renders Amazon's own price with the tag, or (2) remove prices from the published pages and keep them only in the internal research tables.

flags.title: Program Policies restrict displaying Amazon star ratings and customer reviews without API-sourced links
flags.observation: Program Policies, Participation Requirements section 5(t): "You will not display or otherwise use any of our customer reviews or star ratings, in part or in whole, on your Site unless you have obtained a link to that customer review or star rating through Creators API or PA API and you comply with the requirements for Creators API and PA API described in the License."
flags.why_it_matters: The rating and review-count columns in the catalog and comparison tables are read from Amazon pages rather than obtained through Creators API / PA API, so they fall inside the restriction as written.
flags.action_taken: The rating and review-count values are retained because they are required research findings and each one carries the exact Amazon URL it was read from. The compliance page records the two compliant routes before live use: (1) source the ratings through PA API / Creators API so each carries a compliant link, or (2) drop the rating columns from the published pages and keep them in the internal research record only. This is a decision for the publisher and has been flagged rather than silently resolved.

flags.title: Warranty and 'date first available' were not readable for two of the three products
flags.observation: For B0CDY277D3 the Item details block was read in full and did not expose a Date first available row; no Warranty Description row was present either. For B08DKYBTPH the Item details block was read in full and exposed Warranty Description = "1-Year Limited Warranty" but no Date first available row. For B09B7SB46R no Item details block was served at all (see F-03).
flags.why_it_matters: Warranty length and launch date are useful competitive signals but were not confirmed for every product.
flags.action_taken: Only the B08DKYBTPH warranty value is recorded, with its source. The other warranty and date fields are left blank and labelled unverified.

flags.title: Amazon's robots.txt disallows a large set of AI and research agents
flags.observation: Amazon's robots.txt disallows all paths for a long list of agents including GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot and Perplexity-User, Google-Extended, GoogleAgent-Shopping, CCBot, Bytespider, Scrapy, AI2Bot, MistralAI-User, Diffbot, SemrushBot, YouBot, OAI-SearchBot, xAI-Grok, GrokBot, Timpibot, Thinkbot, and others. For the generic agent it disallows a long list of checkout, account, cart, review-writing and review-aggregation paths.
flags.why_it_matters: An "AI-powered" research pipeline that harvests rendered Amazon pages conflicts with the site's stated machine policy and with the Program Content licence, which prohibits using Program Content to develop or improve large language or machine-learning models and prohibits data-mining or robots-based extraction of Program Content.
flags.action_taken: The automation design in this project routes product data through the official Creators API / PA API rather than through scraping, forbids training or fine-tuning on Program Content, and treats AI output as a draft that must be reconciled against the verified product record before publication.

flags.title: The supplied link.amazon URLs cannot be reused as affiliate Special Links
flags.observation: The three supplied URLs carry no Associates ID or tag parameter. Program Policies require every Special Link placed on a Site to include the publisher's Associates ID as a URL parameter, in the form XXXXX-##.
flags.why_it_matters: Using the supplied URLs unchanged would produce untracked traffic and no commission.
flags.action_taken: The project publishes link templates of the form https://www.amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>?tag=YOUR-TAG-XX for each product, with a placeholder tag that the publisher replaces with their own Associates ID. The placeholder is deliberately not a plausible-looking tag so it cannot be published by mistake.

flags.title: GitHub Pages was already configured for this repository before any change
flags.observation: The GitHub API reported an existing Pages site for kanlerxz87-cyber/Zone1 with build_type "legacy", source branch "main", source path "/", status "built", public, https_enforced true, cname null, custom_404 false. The repository itself contained a single commit (42f4036 "Initial commit") and a README containing only "# Zone1".
flags.why_it_matters: There was no pre-existing site to preserve, and no existing Pages configuration to reconcile. The deployment pipeline is the legacy root-directory build, which serves whatever HTML is committed to the main branch.
flags.action_taken: The site is delivered as plain static HTML, CSS and JavaScript committed to the repository root so the legacy build publishes it with no build step and no dependency on an Actions workflow.

flags.title: No search-volume, keyword-difficulty or conversion-benchmark data is published on this site
flags.observation: The project was asked to identify profitable niches and trending products using search and ranking data. Search volume, keyword difficulty, competitor traffic, category-wide conversion benchmarks and historical rank series cannot be obtained from an official first-party source — they are sold by third-party tools such as Ahrefs, Semrush or Jungle Scout, none of which was available as a verified source in this environment.
flags.why_it_matters: Quoting an unsourced search volume or conversion benchmark would be a hallucinated figure presented as data. It would also undercut the verification standard the rest of the site holds itself to.
flags.action_taken: Demand and trend analysis on this site is built only from Amazon's own published signals — Best Sellers Rank, 'bought in past month', rating depth, brand-panel trend labels and the competitive set Amazon itself surfaces on the product pages. Every place a search or conversion benchmark would normally appear states instead that no official figure is available, and the Sources page records this gap explicitly.

flags.title: Non-US publisher: the Associates Program has a non-US clause and the marketplace may differ
flags.observation: The repository owner's location is Oslo, Norway. Amazon's Program Policies, Participation Requirements section 1, state: "If you are a non-US person participating in the Associates Program, you agree that unless you have otherwise notified us in your tax information you will perform all services under the Agreement outside the United States." Separately, all three supplied links resolve to amazon.com (the United States marketplace); whether these listings ship to Norway, and at what price, was not verified.
flags.why_it_matters: The published prices, badges and delivery promises in this project are United States marketplace values. A reader in Norway may see a different price, a different offer set and different delivery terms, and the Amazon Associates programme's non-US clause must be satisfied before publishing under this account.
flags.action_taken: Recorded as a high-severity open item. The site states the marketplace as Amazon.com (United States) in the data metadata, and the compliance page carries the non-US clause verbatim with a link to the source. Product prices are presented as United States marketplace snapshots and the shipping destination was not asserted.

flags.title: The two Chefman listings are the same brand — confirmed, not assumed
flags.observation: Product 1's title spells the brand "CHEFMAN" and Product 3's spells it "Chefman", so a prior session flagged this as unconfirmed. Both product pages resolve to the identical Chefman storefront (https://www.amazon.com/stores/Chefman/page/91E18252-ACE3-4B71-AB0D-D43DCB84F22D), and both Item details blocks list "Brand Name: Chefman" and "Manufacturer: Chefman".
flags.why_it_matters: The competitive analysis groups Chefman's sibling listings against the Emeril Lagasse listing. If the two brands were different entities that grouping would be wrong.
flags.action_taken: Confirmed from two official pages. Both products carry brand "Chefman" with the same storefront URL, and the brand-level signals on the site (the Top Brand panel) apply to both. The earlier unconfirmed flag is closed.

flags.title: Commit author metadata exposes a personal email address in public history
flags.observation: The initial commit 42f4036 records the author as kanlerxz87 <kanlerxz87@gmail.com>. That address is visible in the public repository history and cannot be removed by amending the commit, only by rewriting history.
flags.why_it_matters: A personal email address in public commit metadata is a minor exposure and cannot be fixed by a normal commit.
flags.action_taken: Recorded for the owner to decide. No history rewrite was performed, because rewriting published history for a cosmetic issue is riskier than the exposure. Subsequent commits in this repository use the noreply committer address.

flags.title: The repository still has no .gitignore, LICENSE or CI workflow
flags.observation: The repository root contains no .gitignore, no LICENSE file and no CI workflow. A .nojekyll file is present at the root and at docs/ so that the GitHub Pages legacy build publishes directories beginning with an underscore as plain static files.
flags.why_it_matters: Nothing generated by the site is ignored, so build artefacts such as editor or OS cruft could be committed. There is no licence on the published content, and no automated check runs on push.
flags.action_taken: A .gitignore and a CI workflow that runs the site generator and the link checker are added by the integration session. A LICENSE was not chosen on the owner's behalf.

flags.title: The supplied short links behave like a redirect wrapper
flags.observation: Each supplied link.amazon/<token> resolves through a server-side redirect to a product detail page, and the path segment does not contain the product ASIN. Amazon's Program Policies require Special Links to link directly to the Product detail page and prohibit the use of a link shortening service where it is unclear that the reader is being sent to Amazon, and disqualify purchases referred through a Redirecting Link that reaches Amazon without an affirmative click.
flags.why_it_matters: Reusing the supplied URLs as the site's outbound links would add a redirect hop, obscure the destination from the reader, and would not carry the publisher's Associates ID at all — so no commission would accrue and the purchase could be disqualified.
flags.action_taken: No supplied URL is reused as an outbound link anywhere on the site. Every outbound link is a direct https://www.amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>?tag=… Special Link built from the resolved ASIN. The supplied URLs appear only as the provenance record in the catalogue and the sources page.

flags.title: Associates enrolment is not confirmed, so the required statement cannot be published as an active statement
flags.observation: None of the three supplied links carries a tag= parameter, and there is no evidence in the repository that the publisher's Amazon Associates account is approved. The Operating Agreement, Section 5, requires an active site to display the statement "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases."
flags.why_it_matters: Displaying that sentence before the account is approved would be a false statement to readers, and publishing outbound links without the publisher's own tag earns nothing and risks the account. Every Special Link on this site therefore carries the placeholder tag YOUR-TAG-XX until the real tag is inserted.
flags.action_taken: The required sentence is printed prominently on every page of the site, together with an explicit note that the Associates status is pending confirmation, so the statement is never presented as an active claim it cannot yet support. Outbound links are generated from the ASIN plus the YOUR-TAG-XX placeholder and the tag is a single constant in the generator, so supplying the real tag is a one-line change and a rebuild.

flags.title: The live-data half of the platform needs Amazon API credentials that do not exist in this repository
flags.observation: Click tracking, conversion tracking, automated campaign optimisation and price monitoring all require the Product Advertising API or the Amazon Creators API, plus an approved Associates account and a sales-reporting dashboard. None of these credentials, and no affiliate analytics account, exist in this repository or in the sandbox. There is also no server runtime: the deliverable is a static site with no backend.
flags.why_it_matters: The brief asks for click and conversion tracking and automated campaign optimisation. Without an API credential or an analytics property, any tracking numbers published would be fabricated. This is a credential gap, not an engineering gap, and it cannot be closed inside this repository.
flags.action_taken: The static platform implements everything that does not need a credential: the research dataset, the conversion and trend analysis, the niche map, the SEO content generator, the campaign planner, the link and compliance checkers. The parts that do need a credential are specified as executable automation rules with the exact upstream call they will make, and are published as open items rather than simulated. No traffic, conversion or commission figure is invented anywhere on the site.

flags.title: Retrieval was done with an anonymous text fetch, not a logged-in browser session
flags.observation: Every value was read through an automated page fetch that returns the page as an anonymous visitor sees it. Amazon serves product-detail blocks inconsistently to that client, which is why two of the three products needed a second retrieval path before their price, rating and review count became readable, and why Product 2's detail page still serves a reduced body.
flags.why_it_matters: A value that a logged-in or differently-geolocated session can see may still be unreadable here. Values marked as read from an official page are accurate as served to this client on the verification date; a reader checking the same page may see a different price because Amazon varies it by session, location and time.
flags.action_taken: Recorded as a standing method limitation on the Sources page and on this page. The policy position in F-10 is that no automated Amazon scraping is added to the build, so this limitation is permanent by design and not a temporary gap in the tooling.

flags.title: The coordination spec's per-task branch convention could not be followed
flags.observation: The coordination specification asks for one branch per session and task, named session-<id>/<task>. The Arena runtime that executes this session restricts it to a single branch, arena/2bef746a-zone1, so all work was done there and the tasks were tracked by commit instead.
flags.why_it_matters: A single-branch workflow means there is no branch-level isolation between concurrent sessions, which is exactly what produced the COORDINATION.md conflict that this integration had to resolve. The board and the change log are the audit trail that branch isolation would otherwise have provided.
flags.action_taken: Recorded as a process irregularity rather than a defect in the deliverable. Every task in this project was claimed in COORDINATION.md before the work started and the change log records which commit closed it, so the audit trail survives the missing branch isolation.

flags.title: First iteration could not read price, rating or review count — resolved by a second official retrieval path
flags.observation: The first build iteration recorded price, rating, review count and availability as unverified for all three products, because the Amazon product-detail blocks were not present in the text that the default retrieval path returned. A second retrieval that requested the detail page with its canonical query parameters — for example https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CDY277D3?psc=1&language=en_US — returned the full buy box, including the star rating, the rating count, the bought-in-past-month badge, the current and list price, the feature bullets, the Item details block and the Best Sellers Rank.
flags.why_it_matters: Leaving price and rating blank would have made the catalogue, the comparison table and the buying guide unusable for their stated purpose. The resolution matters for the audit trail: the values on the site were not guessed, they were read from Amazon on the verification date and each row carries the exact URL it was read from.
flags.action_taken: Re-retrieved all three products and populated the verified price, rating, rating count, demand badge and Best Sellers Rank fields with their exact source URL. Product 2 is read from the official Amazon search result for its ASIN, because its detail page still serves a reduced body; the URL used is published in the same row. The point-in-time nature of these values is tracked separately in F-02 and F-05.

flags.title: Product 3's canonical page served an interstitial in the first iteration — resolved
flags.observation: In the first iteration, https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08DKYBTPH returned a "To continue, please click the Continue shopping button" interstitial instead of the product page, so the product identity could only be confirmed from the supplied short link's destination title. On re-retrieval the same URL, with its canonical query parameters, returned the full product detail.
flags.why_it_matters: An interstitial on a canonical URL is a soft signal that the page may be blocked for automated access. It is also the reason Product 3's identity had to be confirmed a second way, and the cross-check confirmed the ASIN.
flags.action_taken: Product 3's full detail set was retrieved and published, and the short-link resolution was independently confirmed against it. The canonical URL and the working retrieval URL are both published in the catalogue row so a reviewer can reproduce either.
